summary: Benign verdict (confidence 0.85) for prof.kaya@aegean.edu. F3 records 10 sign-ins from Portugal via corporate VPN on device LT-3104. Five claims were rejected: TR event is non-interactive mail sync, Turkcell ASN is shared organisational egress, VPN firmware versions include KEV fixes, and vpn-edge-01 had no sign-ins for this account. No compromise signal survived Critic review.

rejected_claims.claim: Suspicious sign-ins from an ASN outside the account's baseline: Turkcell (TR), 1 event(s)

rejected_claims.claim: Password spray then success: 193.140.10.21 failed against 54 accounts (60 failures) and later signed in as this user
rejected_claims.reason: critic: 193.140.10.21 looks like shared egress: 201 distinct accounts completed MFA from this IP in the last 30 days (threshold 10); failures across many accounts are expected background noise, not a coordinated spray

rejected_claims.claim: VPN appliance vpn-edge-02 (firmware 22.7R2.8) runs a product listed in CISA KEV (CVE-2026-104935, CVE-2025-22457, CVE-2025-0282, …)
rejected_claims.reason: critic: firmware 22.7R2.8 already includes the fixes for the KEV entries we can version-check (CVE-2025-22457, CVE-2025-0282)

rejected_claims.reason: critic: vpn-edge-01 did not carry a sign-in for prof.kaya@aegean.edu; its KEV status is not relevant to this account's exposure

risk.rationale: All suspicious signals for prof.kaya@aegean.edu have been rejected with specific, evidence-based explanations: (1) the TR event is a non-interactive ExchangeSync/15 mail-sync token, not a human sign-in; PT sign-ins originate via the university VPN vpn-edge-02 from known device LT-3104, negating impossible travel; (2) the Turkcell/TR ASN and IP 193.140.10.21 are the organization's shared egress/NAT/mail relay (201 distinct accounts MFA'd from it in 30 days), not a new personal network or coordinated spray; (3) vpn-edge-02 firmware 22.7R2.8 already includes fixes for the cited CISA KEV CVEs, and vpn-edge-01 never carried a sign-in for this account. The only verified finding is F3 (LIKELY 0.5: most sign-ins from PT, 10 events), which is consistent with legitimate remote VPN use by the academic and carries no confirmed takeover indicators. No data-quality conflicts remain. Suspicious signals are explained away; no confirmed account takeover chain, no unexplained weak signal, and no exposure requiring human escalation.
